summary: IS DISTINCT FROM compares values while treating NULL as a comparable missing value.
documentation: IS DISTINCT FROM compares values while treating NULL as a comparable missing value. Two NULL values are not distinct; exactly one NULL is distinct. The result is always a Boolean integer rather than an unknown NULL comparison result.
inputs: changes(id INTEGER, before TEXT, after TEXT), containing text or NULL.
returns: id and changed, ordered by id.
caution: Ordinary != produces NULL when either operand is NULL, which can hide changes in filters. Collations and type affinity affect other comparisons; this exercise uses the default text collation.
scenarios: Detect edits from a missing value to a filled value.
Audit imported before/after text including cleared fields.
Compare nullable staging columns without silently losing NULL transitions.
title: Compare nullable field changes
problem: Return id and before IS DISTINCT FROM after AS changed from changes, ordered by id. Return 1 for different text or a one-sided NULL, and 0 for equal text or two NULLs.
hint: Use the NULL-aware distinctness operator rather than !=.
goal: Use IS DISTINCT FROM or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
starter:
-- Write one SELECT or WITH query against the supplied tables.
SELECT 1;
